evals.prompt: Create a self-contained Typst source file for Typst 0.13.1. It should be a one-page experiment summary with a reversed three-item numbered list and inline JSON data decoded from bytes. Save the source as report.typ and provide a short compatibility handoff.
evals.expected_output: A compiling Typst 0.13.1 document that uses only 0.13-compatible APIs and reports the selected common and 0.13 references.
expectations: The handoff resolves the exact target as Typst 0.13.1 and identifies both common topic references and the Typst 0.13 version reference.
The source uses enum reversed behavior and a top-level json(bytes(...)) call rather than a deprecated json.decode call.
The source does not use 0.14- or 0.15-only APIs such as title, frac.style, page.bleed, divider, text.variations, selector.within, list.marker-align, or range.inclusive.
The generated report.typ compiles successfully with Typst 0.13.1.

evals.prompt: Create a self-contained Typst 0.14.2 document called formula-note.typ. Use the 0.14 title element and show a skewed fraction. Include a short compatibility handoff and do not use features from Typst 0.15.
evals.expected_output: A compiling Typst 0.14.2 document that deliberately uses title and frac.style while excluding 0.15-only APIs.
expectations: The handoff resolves the exact target as Typst 0.14.2 and identifies both common topic references and the Typst 0.14 version reference.
The source uses the Typst 0.14 title element and a fraction with style set to skewed.
The source does not use 0.15-only APIs such as page.bleed, divider, text.variations, selector.within, list.marker-align, or range.inclusive.
The generated formula-note.typ compiles successfully with Typst 0.14.2.

evals.prompt: Create a self-contained Typst 0.15.1 print proof named print-proof.typ. Configure 3mm page bleed, add a thematic divider, and show an inclusive numeric range. Provide a short compatibility handoff.
evals.expected_output: A compiling Typst 0.15.1 document using page.bleed, divider, and range.inclusive with explicit version evidence.
expectations: The handoff resolves the exact target as Typst 0.15.1 and identifies both common topic references and the Typst 0.15 version reference.
The source configures page bleed to 3mm, calls divider, and constructs a range with inclusive: true.
The source uses forward slashes for every file path if any paths are present.
The generated print-proof.typ compiles successfully with Typst 0.15.1.

evals.prompt: Create a self-contained Typst project-status.typ document in this workspace without choosing a Typst version for me. Detect the available compiler, include a divider between summary and details when supported, and provide a short compatibility handoff.
evals.expected_output: Detect the compiler actually available in the evaluation workspace, choose compatible features, and report exact evidence.
expectations: The detected version is established by running the workspace compiler, not by assuming 0.15.1.
The selected version reference matches the detected compiler.
The source uses divider only if the detected version supports it; otherwise it uses a compatible separator.
The generated source compiles with the detected compiler.

evals.prompt: Create inherited-features.typ for Typst 0.15.1. Use the dedicated title element, skewed fractions, and str.normalize to show that a decomposed accented letter normalizes to the composed form. Explain which version reference establishes each feature and compile the result.
evals.expected_output: A verified 0.15.1 document using the inherited 0.14 features with the correct reference route.
expectations: The source uses title, a skewed math fraction, and str.normalize.
The handoff identifies the 0.14 feature reference and the 0.15 target reference.
The document compiles with 0.15.1 and the normalization assertion succeeds.

evals.prompt: Create portable.typ, a one-page status report that compiles unchanged on all stable Typst releases from 0.13.0 through 0.15.1. Include a captioned table, a curve drawing, a tiling fill, and inline JSON decoded from bytes. Use the supplied compilers to verify every release. Report exactly which versions were checked.
evals.expected_output: One common-subset source verified by all seven compilers with no removed or later-only API.
expectations: A single source uses curve, tiling, a captioned table, and a top-level JSON bytes loader.
The same source compiles with all seven exact stable releases.
The handoff distinguishes compilation evidence from identical rendering.

evals.prompt: Migrate migration.typ from Typst 0.13.1 to 0.15.1 and save migrated.typ. Replace removed drawing, tiling, and data-decoding APIs and symbol names. Preserve the content and explain the replacements. Compile with 0.15.1.
evals.expected_output: The supplied old source is migrated using current supported counterparts.
expectations: The old drawing path, pattern, and json.decode usages are replaced.
The old sect and plus.circle symbols use supported replacements.
The migrated file compiles with 0.15.1 and retains the values and three sections.

evals.prompt: Fix existing.typ for Typst 0.15.1 and save fixed.typ. The document needs a landscape A4 page with a page-reference supplement and a captioned table, followed by a floating image across both columns. Fix the invalid options without removing the existing headings, labels, caption text, or data. Compile the result.
evals.expected_output: A corrected, compiling existing document with valid page, figure, and image arguments.
expectations: The source retains landscape A4 and uses a supported page supplement value.
The captioned table and image use valid kind, scope, and positional source arguments.
The original headings, labels, captions, and table data remain.
The fixed document compiles with 0.15.1.

evals.prompt: In this environment no Typst compiler can be executed. Create unavailable.typ for a simple two-section PDF-oriented report without an explicit version request. Use only the skill's references; do not run or install a compiler. Provide the intended command and distinguish assumed target, documentation checks, and unperformed compilation.
evals.expected_output: Source with an assumed 0.15.1 target and honest no-compiler verification limits.
expectations: The handoff says 0.15.1 is an assumed target, not a detected compiler.
It explicitly states that compilation and visual verification were not performed.
The source is returned and a usable intended compile command is supplied.

evals.prompt: Create paper.typ for Typst 0.15.1: an A5 report with a table of contents, numbered headings, one footnote, a captioned table of 60 numbered observations with a repeating header, and an IEEE bibliography citing knuth1984 from references.bib. Include a short Korean/English paragraph using an available Korean font. Make the long table break across pages. Compile and inspect the output.
evals.expected_output: A readable multipage paper with references, repeated headers, visible Korean text, and complete data.
expectations: The report includes the outline, footnote, numbered headings, citation, and bibliography.
All 60 observations appear and the header repeats on continuation pages.
A Korean-capable font is selected from the available environment and Korean text remains visible.
The document compiles with 0.15.1 and the handoff reports actual output inspection.

evals.prompt: Create slides.typ for Typst 0.13.0 as three static 16:9 PDF slides about an experiment: overview, method, results. Use a reusable slide function, visible slide numbers, a two-column method slide with the supplied diagram.svg, and a short equation on the results slide. Do not use external packages. Compile and check that there are exactly three slides with no initial blank page.
evals.expected_output: A three-page 16:9 deck compatible with 0.13.0 and a verification handoff.
expectations: The source uses a reusable slide function and no external package.
There are exactly three 16:9 pages with visible slide numbers and no blank first page.
The method slide has two columns and the results slide contains an equation.
The deck compiles with 0.13.0 and actual page checks are reported.
